title: Fully homomorphic encryption from public-key encryption
formal: Does the existence of IND-CPA-secure public-key bit encryption imply the existence of an IND-CPA-secure, compact, unleveled fully homomorphic bit-encryption scheme for every polynomial-size Boolean circuit, with the algorithms and security convention below?
definitions:
All algorithms are uniform probabilistic Turing machines with worst-case polynomial bit running time in their explicit input lengths; decryption is deterministic. The security parameter \(\lambda\) is supplied in unary. An adversary is a nonuniform family of randomized Boolean circuits of size polynomial in \(\lambda\), including its advice and random-input nodes. All random bits are independent and fair. A function \(
u :N	o [0,1]\) is negligible when for every positive integer a there exists \(\lambda _{0}\) such that \(
u (\lambda )\le \lambda ^{- a}\) for all \(\lambda \ge \lambda _{0}\). Security is quantified separately over every such adversary family, with a negligible bound allowed to depend on the family. A public-key bit-encryption scheme consists of \(Gen(1^{\lambda})=(pk,sk), Enc(pk,b)=c\) for \(b\in \{0,1\}\), and \(Dec(sk,c)\in \{0,1,\perp\}\). There is one negligible \(
u\) such that for every \(\lambda\) and b, Pr[Dec(\(sk,Enc(pk,b)\))≠b]\(\le 
u (\lambda )\), over key generation and encryption. In the IND-CPA experiment Gen is run, the adversary receives pk and selects bits \(b_{0},b_{1}\) and a state, an independent uniform \( eta \in \{0,1\}\) is chosen, \(c=Enc(pk,b_{ eta})\) is returned, and the adversary outputs \( eta '\). Require |\(\Pr [ eta ' = eta ]- 1/2|\) to be negligible. The adversary may perform any polynomial number of public encryptions on its own before and after the challenge. There is no decryption oracle. Bit encryption suffices; longer messages are represented by bit lists. For FHE, Gen outputs (pk,evk,sk); the evaluation key evk is public and is included with pk in the IND-CPA experiment. Gen receives no circuit size or depth bound. Eval(evk,\(C,c_{1},\ldots ,c_{t}\)) outputs one ciphertext for a circuit \(C:\{0,1\}^{t}	o \{0,1\}\), encoded as an acyclic \(\mathrm{AND}/\mathrm{OR}/\mathrm{NOT}\) circuit with listed wires. For every polynomial s there is a negligible \(
u _{s}\) such that for every \(\lambda\), every such C of description length and input count at most \(s(\lambda )\), and every \(m\in \{0,1\}^{t}\), independently of the generated keys, Pr[Dec(sk,Eval(evk,\(C,Enc(pk,m_{1}),\ldots ,Enc(pk,m_{t})\)))≠\(C(m)\)]\(\le 
u _{s}(\lambda )\). The probability includes key generation, fresh encryption coins for each bit, and evaluation coins. Eval’s time is polynomial in the entire supplied circuit and ciphertext encoding, with one algorithm for all C. There is one polynomial q, independent of C,t and s, bounding every evaluated ciphertext length and its decryption time by \(q(\lambda )\); keys also have polynomial length. The scheme must also correctly decrypt fresh encryptions. Multiple output bits mean separate output ciphertexts, so compactness scales linearly with output length. Only the usual one-evaluation correctness contract is required; no circuit privacy or additional guarantee for arbitrary malformed or previously evaluated ciphertexts is imposed. The assertion is an existence implication between these two primitives in the classical standard model; it permits non-black-box constructions and supplies no extra setup, ideal oracle, circular-security or number-theoretic assumption.

context_blocks.text: Public-key encryption permits confidential communication; fully homomorphic encryption additionally permits computation over ciphertexts. A general implication would make the stronger capability follow from the existence of the basic public-key primitive.

The cited black-box separation rules out deriving fully homomorphic encryption from even hierarchical identity-based encryption by that restricted type of construction. It therefore supplies a barrier and motivation, not a negative answer to an arbitrary non-black-box implication. The existing LWE-to-FHE card starts from a specific stronger assumption.

why: Determine whether computation over encrypted data requires fundamentally more than public-key confidentiality.
answer_criterion: Prove the existence implication with full correctness, compactness and security for the defined schemes, or refute that implication. A leveled construction whose key generation needs a depth bound, an additional cryptographic assumption, or only a black-box impossibility result does not settle it.
